chapter.title: Electrical Machinery and Equipment and Parts Thereof; Sound Recorders and Reproducers, Television Image and Sound Recorders and Reproducers, and Parts and Accessories of Such Articles

page.h1: HTS Chapter 85: Electrical Machinery and Equipment and Parts Thereof; Sound Recorders and Reproducers, Television Image and Sound Recorders and Reproducers, and Parts and Accessories of Such Articles — U.S. Export FAQ

seo.title: U.S. Electrical Machinery Export FAQ (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Common questions about exporting electrical machinery, electronics and semiconductors: foreign tariffs, export licenses and Schedule B codes.

intro: Short answers to real questions people search about exporting U.S. electrical machinery and electronics, with a link to the page that has the detail.
keyTakeaways: Canada and China are the two major buyers charging more than in January 2025: Canada 25%–50% on a list of U.S. phones, network gear, monitors, appliances, parts and cable since September 2026, and China a flat 10% extra on all U.S. goods.
For advanced semiconductors, a U.S. export licence — not a foreign tariff — is usually the real obstacle.
Mexico, the EU, South Korea and Hong Kong all charge nothing on U.S. goods in this chapter.
questionSource: Google search-suggestion queries for "china tariff on us chips", "export license semiconductor", "schedule b code integrated circuits", "tariff on us electronics to eu", "do i need eei for electronics export", and "canada tariff on us appliances".

faqs.question: Does China charge extra tariffs on U.S. semiconductors?
faqs.answer: Yes. China's own MFN rate on most chips is already 0% under the WTO Information Technology Agreement, but China adds a flat 10% extra duty on all U.S.-origin goods, in force since May 2025. That 10% is the entire increase since January 2025 for semiconductors.

faqs.question: What tariff does the EU charge on U.S. electronics?
faqs.answer: Nothing, from July 1, 2026. Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroed out the EU's remaining tariffs on this chapter under the EU–U.S. framework; most chips, phones and storage media were already at 0% before that under the WTO Information Technology Agreement.

faqs.question: Do I need an export license to ship semiconductors?
searchedAs: do i need a license to export chips
faqs.answer: It depends on the chip. Most commercial semiconductors are EAR99 and need no licence. Certain high-performance computing chips carry ECCN 3A090 and need a BIS licence for China and dozens of other destinations regardless of value — check the Commerce Control List before you ship.

faqs.question: What is the Schedule B code for integrated circuits?
faqs.answer: Integrated circuits fall under Schedule B heading 8542, the same first four digits as the HS/HTS code. Look up the exact 10-digit Schedule B number for your specific chip with the Census Bureau's free search tool; it also tells you which line of the buyer's tariff schedule applies.

faqs.question: Did Canada add new tariffs on U.S. electronics or appliances?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since September 8, 2026 Canada charges a 50% counter-tariff on U.S. smartphones (8517.13), routers, switches and other data-transmission apparatus (8517.62) and other monitors (8528.59.90), and 25% on other domestic appliances (8509.80), domestic cooking appliances (8516.60), parts for TV, radio and monitor apparatus (8529.90) and insulated conductors for 1,000 V or less (8544.49). The list has no exemption for goods that qualify for CUSMA: it applies to all U.S.-origin goods on it. Chips, semiconductors, motors, batteries and most industrial electrical machinery are not on the list and still enter duty-free under CUSMA.

faqs.question: How much electrical machinery and electronics does the U.S. export?
searchedAs: how much does the us export in electrical machinery
faqs.answer: $226.05B in 2025, up 5.7% on 2024 — the third-largest of the chapters these reports cover, after mineral fuels (Chapter 27) and machinery (Chapter 84). Integrated circuits (23% of the total) and smartphones and network equipment (21%) are the two biggest categories.

faqs.question: Who buys the most U.S. semiconductors?
searchedAs: who buys the most us chips
faqs.answer: Mexico and Canada, the two USMCA partners, together took 38% of all U.S. Chapter 85 exports in 2025 — much of it feeding integrated North American electronics supply chains. China is the third-largest single-country buyer.

faqs.question: Do I need to file EEI for a chip shipment?
searchedAs: do i need to file eei for chips
faqs.answer: File EEI once a Schedule B number in a shipment to one buyer exceeds $2,500 — the normal export threshold — and at any value if the chip needs a BIS export licence, which many advanced computing chips do.

faqs.question: Is Mexico's tariff on U.S. electronics 0%?
faqs.answer: Yes, for goods that meet USMCA's rules of origin and travel with a valid certificate of origin. Mexico is this chapter's largest single market, and almost all of that trade enters duty-free.

faqs.question: What happens when China's tariff suspension on U.S. goods ends?
faqs.answer: China's current 10% blanket extra duty on U.S. goods runs through a one-year suspension of 24 points that China and the U.S. agreed to extend to January 10, 2027. If it is not extended again, the rate would jump back to 34% on top of each heading's normal MFN rate.
